To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
neural machine translation models can be used to predict typological information for thousands of languages.

(1) neural machine translation can be used to predict typological features of languages; (2) the model is able to infer information about phonological and phonemic inventories, as well as about syntax; (3) the model is competitive with a baseline that has knowledge of the languages geographic and linguistic neighbors.

we can predict information missing from the typological database by training a many to one NLP system from a language into English, and the predictions are better than a baseline that has information about the language's geographic and phylogenetically neighbors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: can we use neural models to learn language representations for typological prediction?

the following two questions: (i) What can we learn about language typology from a large-scale NMT system that is trained on a massive number of parallel texts? (ii) Can we use this knowledge to improve typological classification and fill in missing data in the typological databases?
the question of what knowledge neural machine translation models have of the languages they are trained on.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the NMT model learns to predict the typological features with an accuracy of about 50%, which is a very good result considering that the features are predicted in a zero-shot manner, i.e., without any training data for the languages in question.
the neural model is able to learn a lot about languages and that it is possible to extract this information from the model to fill holes in the existing typological databases.
the proposed method has the ability to predict information missing in typological databases and that the proposed method improves over a baseline.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can learn a lot from a neural machine translation model, and we can use it to predict typological information about languages.
the proposed method can be used to extract typological features from a large amount of unannotated data.
we show how to use NMT to extract information that is missing from typological data sets, and to infer features about languages that are difficult to obtain from human experts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
neural NMT models can learn a lot about the languages they translate, and that the knowledge can be used to predict information about languages for which there are few or no parallel texts.
NMT systems can be leveraged for typology prediction, and that the resulting systems can be used as an alternative way to collect data for typological studies.
neural models are capable of learning and extracting information about language structure, which is useful to linguistics and NLP.
